title: REET 2026 - Rajasthan Teacher Eligibility Test
meta_description: REET 2026 Level 1 (Classes 1–5) & Level 2 (6–8). Lifetime validity. 7,700+ vacancies. No negative marking. 60% to pass.

hero.one_liner: Rajasthan teacher eligibility test - mandatory for government school teaching in Rajasthan. Level 1 (primary) and Level 2 (upper primary).

what_is_it: REET (Rajasthan Eligibility Examination for Teachers) conducted by Board of Secondary Education, Rajasthan (BSER) certifies eligibility for government school teaching. Level 1: Classes 1–5 (primary). Level 2: Classes 6–8 (upper primary). One of India's most competitive teacher exams - 30+ lakh applicants annually, larger than many national exams. Passing REET is first gate; subsequent Rajasthan 3rd Grade Teacher recruitment exam determines actual appointment.

REET comprises 150 MCQs in 2.5 hours with NO negative marking - attempt all questions. Syllabus: Child Development & Pedagogy (30 Qs), Language 1 & 2 (60 Qs), Mathematics (30 Qs), EVS/Social Studies (30 Qs). Qualifying marks: 60% for General (90/150), 55% for OBC/SC/ST. Lifetime validity (changed from 3-year limit in 2021) is major advantage - pass once, appear for recruitment exams anytime in future.

For Rajasthan residents, particularly those with teaching aptitude, REET is a direct pathway to secure government job (salary ₹28,000–55,000/month depending on level, plus pension). Teachers command social respect in Rajasthani society. Teaching also allows work-life balance (regular school hours, 2-month summer vacation). Competition is fierce because of these factors - but serious preparation over 4–6 months positions you in successful band (100+ out of 150).

key_details.label: Negative Marking
key_details.value: No negative marking - no penalty for wrong

exam_pattern.description: Single paper, 150 questions, 150 marks, 150 minutes. No negative marking. Pass: 60% (90 marks) for General.

extra_sections.heading: REET Exam Pattern - Level 1 and Level 2 Detailed
content:
REET (Rajasthan Eligibility Examination for Teachers) is conducted in two levels, and understanding the exact pattern is crucial for focused preparation. LEVEL 1 (Classes 1-5, Primary Teacher):
- Total Questions: 150 MCQs
- Total Marks: 150
- Duration: 2 hours 30 minutes
- Sections: Child Development & Pedagogy (30 marks), Language 1 - Hindi (30 marks), Language 2 - English/Sanskrit/Urdu/Sindhi/Punjabi/Gujarati (30 marks), Mathematics (30 marks), Environmental Studies (30 marks)
- No negative marking
- Qualifying marks: 60% (General), 55% (OBC/MBC), 50% (SC/ST)

LEVEL 2 (Classes 6-8, Upper Primary Teacher):
- Total Questions: 150 MCQs
- Total Marks: 150
- Duration: 2 hours 30 minutes
- Sections: Child Development & Pedagogy (30 marks), Language 1 - Hindi (30 marks), Language 2 - English/Sanskrit/Urdu/Sindhi/Punjabi/Gujarati (30 marks), Subject-specific paper - Mathematics & Science OR Social Science (60 marks)
- No negative marking
- Same qualifying percentage as Level 1 IMPORTANT: You can appear for both Level 1 and Level 2 in the same exam cycle.
Clearing both levels makes you eligible to teach Classes 1-8, maximizing your job opportunities. The exam is conducted on separate dates for each level, so there is no scheduling conflict.

extra_sections.heading: How REET leads to a teaching job

steps.title: REET eligibility test
steps.desc: A 150-mark qualifying paper for Level 1 (Classes 1-5) or Level 2 (Classes 6-8). Score the qualifying percentage to pass.

steps.title: Lifetime certificate
steps.desc: Qualifying gives you a REET certificate that is now valid for life. Its marks are not added to the final job merit.

steps.title: REET Mains recruitment
steps.desc: The actual 3rd Grade Teacher recruitment, run by RSMSSB. This 300-mark exam carries negative marking, and your final merit comes only from this stage, not from the eligibility test.

steps.title: 3rd Grade Teacher
steps.desc: Selected candidates join as 3rd Grade Teachers in Rajasthan government schools after document checks and a 2-year probation.

extra_sections.heading: REET vs REET Mains - the two-exam system
content: REET trips up newcomers because it is really two separate exams. Clearing the eligibility test is not the same as landing a teaching job.
Stage one is the REET eligibility test described on this page. Passing it earns a lifetime certificate, but those marks never count toward any job merit.
Stage two is REET Mains, the actual 3rd Grade Teacher recruitment run by RSMSSB. This is the exam that genuinely decides who gets hired.
REET Mains is a 300-mark paper, and unlike the eligibility test it carries negative marking of one-third for wrong answers. Your final merit is built only from this score.
The most recent Mains, held in January 2026, offered 7,759 teacher posts. Competition is sharp, so a safe target sits well above 210 out of 300.
The takeaway is simple. Treat the eligibility test as the gate and the Mains as the real contest, and prepare seriously for both rather than relaxing after you qualify.

items.title: Child Development & Pedagogy (30)
items.sub: Common to both levels and the highest-scoring section. Focus on understanding concepts over rote memorisation, since application-style questions are common and reward real clarity.

items.title: Languages (30 + 30)
items.sub: Language 1 and Language 2 cover grammar, comprehension and the pedagogy of teaching that language. Grammar is the reliable scorer.

items.title: Maths / Science
items.sub: NCERT-level concepts plus the pedagogy of teaching them. For Level 2 science-maths, balance content with teaching methods.

items.title: EVS / Social Studies & Rajasthan GK
items.sub: EVS for Level 1 and Social Studies for Level 2, both heavy on Rajasthan. State history, geography and culture decide many marks, so build a dedicated Rajasthan GK section in your notes.

extra_sections.heading: REET Salary, Benefits, and Career Growth
content: REET only gives the eligibility certificate. The salary below is for the 3rd Grade Teacher post you reach after clearing the REET Mains recruitment.
Both Level 1 and Level 2 teachers sit at Pay Matrix Level 10, so their pay is essentially the same. The real difference is probation versus after probation.
During the 2-year probation, you draw a fixed amount of about ₹23,700 a month, which is roughly ₹20,900 to ₹21,300 in hand after deductions.
After probation, with DA, HRA and other allowances, in-hand pay rises to roughly ₹40,000 to ₹48,000 a month.
Beyond pay, you get RGHS medical cover, a pension, paid leave and time-bound promotions to 2nd Grade and 1st Grade teacher over your career.

items.title: Ignoring pedagogy
items.sub: Many treat REET like a GK quiz and underprepare pedagogy. It is the largest, most scoring and most predictable section.

items.title: Skipping Rajasthan GK
items.sub: State-specific history, geography and culture carry real weight, especially in Social Studies. Generic national GK is not enough.

items.title: Confusing REET with the job
items.sub: Passing REET only gives the certificate. The teaching post needs the separate REET Mains recruitment, so prepare for both and do not ease off after you qualify.

items.title: Targeting only one level
items.sub: If you are eligible for both, appearing in Level 1 and Level 2 widens your chances across more recruitment posts. The extra paper is a small cost for a meaningfully larger pool of jobs to compete for.

extra_sections.heading: REET Eligibility - Who Can Appear?
content: REET eligibility criteria differ slightly for Level 1 and Level 2. Understanding the exact requirements helps you plan your preparation timeline.

LEVEL 1 (Primary Teacher, Classes 1-5):
- Minimum qualification: Senior Secondary (10+2/12th) with at least 50% marks AND Diploma in Elementary Education (D.El.Ed) of 2-year duration, OR Senior Secondary (10+2/12th) with at least 45% marks AND D.El.Ed as per NCTE 2002 norms, OR Senior Secondary (10+2/12th) with at least 50% marks AND 4-year B.El.Ed degree, OR Senior Secondary (10+2/12th) with at least 50% marks AND 2-year D.Ed (Special Education). LEVEL 2 (Upper Primary Teacher, Classes 6-8):
- Minimum qualification: Graduation with at least 50% marks AND B.Ed degree (2-year course), OR Graduation with 45% marks AND B.Ed as per NCTE norms, OR Senior Secondary with 50% marks AND 4-year B.A.B.Ed/B.Sc.B.Ed integrated degree, OR Graduation with 50% marks AND 1-year B.Ed (Special Education).
AGE LIMIT: Minimum 18 years, Maximum 40 years (General), 45 years (OBC/MBC/EBC), 45 years (SC/ST/SBC/Women/Divyang/Ex-servicemen). Age is calculated as on January 1 of the exam year.

IMPORTANT: Final year students of D.El.Ed/B.Ed can also appear for REET provisionally. However, they must produce the final degree/diploma certificate at the time of 3rd Grade Teacher recruitment document verification.

extra_sections.heading: REET Certificate Validity and Updates
content: The REET certificate was originally valid for 3 years from the date of result declaration. However, the Rajasthan government has repeatedly extended validity periods in the past.

In recent policy updates, the government has considered making REET certificates valid for a lifetime, similar to CTET certificates (which were made lifetime valid in 2021). Candidates should check the latest notification on the official REET website (reetbser.com or rajeduboard.rajasthan.gov.in) for the current validity period.

If your certificate is expiring and no recruitment has been announced, you may need to appear for the next REET cycle to maintain eligibility. REET scores are non-transferable - they can only be used for Rajasthan state teacher recruitment.

Unlike CTET, which is accepted by KVS, NVS, and central schools, REET is exclusively for Rajasthan government schools. If you want to teach outside Rajasthan, you will need the respective state TET or CTET qualification.

extra_sections.heading: Best Books and Resources for REET Preparation
content:
CHILD DEVELOPMENT AND PEDAGOGY:
- 'Bal Vikas Evam Shiksha Shastra' by S.P. Gupta (Hindi)
- 'Child Development and Pedagogy' by Disha Publication (English)
- NCERT Psychology textbook for Class 11-12
- Previous year REET/CTET pedagogy questions compiled in book form

HINDI LANGUAGE:
- 'Hindi Bhasha' by Kiran Publication
- NCERT Hindi textbooks for Classes 6-12
- Rajasthan Board Hindi textbooks
- Any standard Hindi grammar book covering Samas, Sandhi, Alankar, Chhand ENGLISH LANGUAGE:
- Wren & Martin 'High School English Grammar and Composition'
- NCERT English textbooks for Classes 6-10
- Any standard English grammar practice book with MCQs

MATHEMATICS:
- NCERT Math textbooks for Classes 1-10 (depending on level)
- 'Mathematics for REET' by Arihant or Youth Competition Times
- R.S. Aggarwal for practice problems

ENVIRONMENTAL STUDIES / SOCIAL SCIENCE:
- NCERT EVS/Social Science textbooks for Classes 3-8
- 'Rajasthan GK' by Rajasthan Chronicle or Lakshya Publication
- 'Rajasthan Ka Itihas' by Ratan Lal Mishra for Rajasthan history ONLINE RESOURCES:
- Utkarsh Classes YouTube channel (free REET lectures in Hindi)
- BYJU's Exam Prep REET section
- Gradeup (now BYJU's Exam Prep) REET mock tests
- reetbser.com for official syllabus, previous papers, and notifications

extra_sections.title: Posts in REET Mains 2026
extra_sections.desc: The January 2026 REET Mains recruitment offered 7,759 3rd Grade Teacher posts across Level 1 and Level 2. The eligibility certificate only lets you compete for these, so qualifying early keeps you ready for the next drive.

extra_sections.heading: REET Exam Day Tips
content: On exam day, reach the center 60 minutes early to avoid last-minute stress. Carry your admit card, Aadhaar card, two passport photos, a black ballpoint pen, and a transparent water bottle.
Read each question carefully - there is no negative marking in REET, so attempt every single question even if you are unsure. Start with your strongest section to build confidence and momentum.

extra_sections.heading: REET qualifying marks by category
content: To pass the REET eligibility test you must clear the qualifying percentage for your category. General candidates need 60%, which works out to 90 marks out of 150.
Reserved categories get relaxations. OBC, SC and EWS candidates typically need about 55%, while ST candidates in TSP areas and the Sahariya tribe need around 36%.
Women and ex-servicemen usually need about 50%, and candidates with disabilities around 40%. Always check the exact slab for your category in the official notification.
The eligibility test traditionally had no negative marking. From 2025, RBSE moved to five answer options and reportedly introduced a one-third penalty, so confirm the scheme for your cycle.
Because the cutoff is a fixed percentage rather than a rank, your goal is clear. Cross your category's bar comfortably and the lifetime certificate is yours, whatever others score.

extra_sections.heading: REET application and fees
content: Applications open online on the RBSE REET portal when a cycle is announced. You fill in personal and academic details, choose your level, and upload a photo and signature.
In the last cycle the fee was around ₹550 for a single level and ₹750 for both levels. Repeat applicants and reserved categories paid less.
You can apply for Level 1, Level 2, or both, depending on your qualifications. Choosing both costs a little more but widens the posts you can target later.
Keep your marksheets, photo and signature ready in the required format before you start. Small upload errors are a common reason forms get rejected.
After paying, download the confirmation page and save your application number. You will need it for the admit card and result stages.
Apply early in the window. The portal slows down badly in the final two days before the deadline.

items.title: History & kingdoms
items.sub: Mewar and the Sisodias, Chittorgarh, Maharana Pratap, and the major Rajput dynasties and their forts.

items.title: Geography
items.sub: The Thar desert and Aravallis, major rivers, districts and climate. Map-based and resource questions are common.

items.title: Art & culture
items.sub: Folk dances, fairs and festivals, miniature painting schools, and famous temples and havelis of the state.

items.title: Polity & schemes
items.sub: State administration, panchayati raj and current Rajasthan government schemes that feed Social Studies and current-affairs questions. A monthly Rajasthan current-affairs habit pays off here.

extra_sections.heading: REET preparation - what actually works
content: Child Development and Pedagogy (30 marks) is common to both levels and is the most scoring section. Focus on Piaget, Vygotsky, Kohlberg theories, learning disabilities, inclusive education, and NCF 2005.

This section is purely theory-based - memorize and practice with previous year papers. For Level 1, focus on Mathematics and Environmental Studies at Class 1-5 level - questions are simple but tricky.
For Level 2, choose either Science-Math or Social Science based on your graduation subject. Science-Math questions are from Class 6-8 NCERT.
Social Science covers History, Geography, Civics, and Economics. Rajasthan GK is crucial - 30 marks in both levels.

Cover Rajasthan history (Rajput kingdoms, freedom movement), geography (Thar desert, Aravalli range, rivers, climate), art and culture (dance forms, forts, festivals), and current affairs. Use 'Rajasthan Samanya Gyan' by Lakshmi Narayan Nathuramka.

extra_sections.heading: REET qualification doesn't guarantee a job
extra_sections.content:
REET is an eligibility test - passing it makes you eligible to apply for Rajasthan teacher vacancies. Actual recruitment is done through a separate merit-based process (3rd grade teacher recruitment) where your REET score, graduation marks, and B.Ed marks are combined.

REET certificate is valid for 3 years from the result date.

extra_sections.heading: Attempt both Level 1 and Level 2
extra_sections.content:
You can attempt both levels in the same exam cycle (they're held on different dates). This doubles your chances - if you don't make the cutoff for Level 2, you might clear Level 1.

Primary teacher positions (Level 1) often have more vacancies and lower competition than upper primary (Level 2).

extra_sections.text: REET is Rajasthan's golden ticket to government teaching - clearing it with a high score means a permanent position with the Rajasthan government, full pension benefits, and the respect that comes with shaping young minds.

preparation_tips: No negative marking = attempt all 150 questions. This is your advantage. Never leave blanks. Even 50-50 guesses give you expected value of 0.5 marks per question (better than 0 for blank). Strategy: (1) Attempt easy questions first (75 questions in 60 min). (2) Medium questions (50 Qs in 40 min). (3) Difficult remaining (25 Qs in 50 min). (4) Final 5 minutes: verify answers.
CTET and REET overlap 80% - if preparing for CTET, appear for REET with minimal extra effort. Add Rajasthan GK (3–4 weeks) and you're ready.

Child Development (30 Qs) is high-weightage - 20% of exam. Topics: Piaget's cognitive development, attachment (Bowlby), emotional intelligence, special needs, inclusive education. These are straightforward if you have studied B.Ed content properly. Score 24+/30 here is achievable with focused revision.

Mock tests from month 2. Take 2–3 full-length mocks per week. Target: 100+/150 (67%) to be safe. Analyze each mock: Which sections took longest? Where did you make silly errors? Which topics are weak?

faqs.question: Is REET lifetime validity really permanent?
faqs.answer:
Yes. As of 2021, REET validity changed to lifetime - no expiry date.

This is huge advantage. Even if you clear REET today but don't get recruited immediately, your REET score remains valid forever.

You can apply for recruitment exams 5, 10, even 20 years later if needed.

faqs.question: Should I target Level 1 or Level 2?
faqs.answer:
Level 2 (₹36,600+ basic) pays significantly more than Level 1 (₹23,700 basic) - ₹13,000/month difference. If you have B.Ed, always target Level 2.

Level 1 is only if you have D.El.Ed but not B.Ed. You can appear for both levels in same exam cycle, so do both.

faqs.question: REET passing guarantee me a job?
faqs.answer:
No. REET is only eligibility gate.

Actual recruitment is through separate Rajasthan 3rd Grade Teacher recruitment exam (conducted by RSMSSB). You must clear both REET (one-time) + Recruitment exam (periodic) to get appointed.

REET score is valid for recruitment exams conducted anytime in future.

faqs.question: What is the REET 2026 exam date?
faqs.answer:
REET 2026 exam date has not been officially announced yet. Check bser.rajasthan.gov.in (Board of Secondary Education Rajasthan) for the latest notification.

Based on previous cycles, the exam is expected in the second half of 2026. Registration typically opens 2-3 months before the exam.

faqs.question: What is the REET passing marks?
faqs.answer:
General category: 60% (90 out of 150 marks). SC/ST/OBC/PwD: 55% (82.5 out of 150, rounded to 83).

These are qualifying marks - you need to score above this to receive the REET certificate. Actual teacher recruitment cutoffs are usually higher than qualifying marks.

faqs.question: Is B.Ed mandatory for REET?
faqs.answer:
For Level 1: D.El.Ed (diploma in elementary education) or B.El.Ed is sufficient. B.Ed is not mandatory.

For Level 2: B.Ed or equivalent is required along with graduation in the relevant subject. Candidates in the final year of B.Ed can also apply provisionally.

faqs.question: What is the full form of REET?
faqs.answer: REET stands for Rajasthan Eligibility Examination for Teachers. It is the eligibility test, conducted by RBSE, that you must pass to be considered for 3rd Grade Teacher posts in Rajasthan.

faqs.question: What is the salary of a teacher after REET?
faqs.answer:
REET only gives the certificate. After also clearing the REET Mains recruitment, you join as a 3rd Grade Teacher at Pay Level 10.

During the 2-year probation you draw about ₹23,700 a month, rising to roughly ₹40,000 to ₹48,000 in hand after probation, with DA, HRA, medical cover and a pension.
